brief: Design an interface for a "Memory Decay Calculator" that helps people with amnesia or memory conditions understand how quickly they might forget newly learned information, visualized as an interactive

dominant_strengths: Glowing orb metaphor for memories evokes fragility and decay, with warning triangles adding emotional tension and stakes.
Dark ambient palette with soft green bioluminescence creates a contemplative, almost neural mood fitting amnesia context.
Color-coded legend (Sleep/Stress/Rehearsal) hints at a thoughtful underlying model of memory factors.
dominant_weaknesses: Massive empty canvas with only three orbs makes the layout feel unfinished and wastes 80% of the screen real estate.
No visible decay timeline, axes, or scale — user cannot actually read 'how quickly' forgetting happens, breaking the brief.
Tiny legend stranded at bottom, lonely 'Create Memory' button top-left, and floating orbs lack any compositional anchor or hierarchy.
fix_priorities: Add a temporal axis or decay curve so orbs map to time-since-learning, making decay legible rather than decorative.
Introduce interactive controls for Sleep/Stress/Rehearsal sliders tied to the visualization to fulfill the 'calculator' promise.
Tighten composition: cluster orbs, add labels/timestamps per memory, and bring the legend into a proper sidebar panel.
Strengthen typography hierarchy — current labels are uniformly small and weightless against the vast dark field.
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral atmosphere is the strongest layer, but behavioral usability is severely under-developed and reflective meaning is hinted at without being earned.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially — the metaphor and mood evoke memory fragility, but it fails as a 'calculator' since no quantitative decay, time axis, or interactive parameter control is visible.
